stem: A client is receiving negative pressure wound therapy. Which complication requires continued monitoring during therapy?

options.A: Temporary flattening of the foam dressing under suction because this finding by itself indicates hemorrhage beneath the dressing.
options.B: Bleeding or hemorrhage from the wound because negative pressure wound therapy has a recognized risk of uncontrolled bleeding.
options.C: Mild operating noise from the therapy unit because any audible pump sound indicates tissue injury and requires immediate discontinuation.
options.D: Gradual collection of expected wound drainage in the canister because any drainage during negative pressure therapy represents a complication.

rationale: FDA identifies uncontrolled bleeding as a recognized risk associated with negative pressure wound therapy and directs labeling to address bleeding and hemorrhage with warnings and precautions. Therefore B is the clinically important complication to monitor. A incorrectly treats dressing contraction under suction as proof of bleeding, C equates ordinary device sound with tissue injury, and D incorrectly classifies expected wound-fluid removal as a complication in itself.
educational_objective: Monitor clients receiving negative pressure wound therapy for bleeding or hemorrhage, a recognized device-related safety risk.

source_claim_supported: FDA identifies uncontrolled bleeding/hemorrhage as an NPWT risk and recommends device safeguards and labeling warnings/precautions addressing this hazard.

source_original.stem: A client is receiving negative pressure wound therapy. Which complication requires continued monitoring during therapy?

options.A: Temporary flattening of the foam dressing under suction, because this finding by itself indicates that hemorrhage is occurring beneath the dressing.
options.B: Bleeding or hemorrhage from the wound, because negative pressure wound therapy has recognized bleeding risks that require ongoing clinical monitoring.
options.C: Mild operating noise from the therapy unit, because any audible pump sound indicates tissue injury and requires immediate discontinuation of therapy.
options.D: Gradual collection of expected wound drainage in the canister, because any drainage during negative pressure therapy represents a treatment complication.

source_original.rationale: FDA identifies bleeding and hemorrhage as important risks of negative pressure wound therapy, so ongoing assessment for bleeding remains necessary. Option B identifies the clinically important complication. Option A treats normal dressing contraction under suction as proof of hemorrhage, which it is not. Option C treats ordinary device sound as evidence of tissue injury without a clinical basis. Option D incorrectly labels any expected wound drainage as a complication rather than assessing the amount and character of drainage and the patient.
source_original.source_detail: FDA Negative Pressure Wound Therapy special-controls guidance — Risks to Health / Labeling precautions: bleeding and hemorrhage are recognized NPWT hazards requiring monitoring and appropriate warnings/precautions. Current FDA NPWT device guidance and safety information at cited URL; rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: asepsis, equipment/environmental safety, incident/event prevention and infection-control activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained key and construct. Tightened the keyed answer to FDA's explicit 'uncontrolled bleeding' risk and verified currentness through the FDA product-classification page updated July 20, 2026.

audit_findings.source_authority: FDA Class II special-controls guidance/current product classification.
audit_findings.currentness: FDA still links this guidance for product code OKO; classification page updated 2026-07-20.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item tests only the explicit bleeding/hemorrhage hazard and avoids unsupported drainage thresholds or device-alarm rules.

distractor_audit.A: Dressing contraction alone is not proof of hemorrhage.
distractor_audit.C: Ordinary sound is not identified as tissue injury.
distractor_audit.D: Fluid removal is part of the device's intended function; drainage alone is not a complication.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B identifies an FDA-recognized complication.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe observable therapy findings; no second defensible answer.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safe equipment use and complication recognition.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Confirmed current FDA status and removed any implication that expected drainage itself is abnormal.
